questions.stemHtml: The constant torque required to accelerate a disk (of rotational inertia I) from rest to a speed of f rotations per second in a time interval t is
questions.stemText: The constant torque required to accelerate a disk (of rotational inertia I) from rest to a speed of f rotations per second in a time interval t is
questions.solution: Convert the final speed to angular speed: $\omega_f=2\pi f$. Since the disk starts from rest, $\alpha=\Delta\omega/t=2\pi f/t$. Therefore $\tau=I\alpha=2\pi fI/t$, so the answer is D.
skillTags: Convert rotations per second to radians per second
questions.trainingFocus: Angular units and the rotational analogue of Newton's second law

questions.stemHtml: Figure 7.4 shows five graphs of angular velocity as a function of time, ω(t). In which graph does the particle have the greatest angular displacement?
questions.stemText: Five graphs show angular velocity as a function of time. In which graph does the particle have the greatest angular displacement?
questions.solution: Angular displacement is $\Delta\theta=\int \omega\,dt$, the signed area under the $\omega$-versus-$t$ graph. Graph B encloses area 1 over the displayed interval, which is larger than the signed area for every other graph. The answer is B.
questions.trainingFocus: Graph-to-quantity translation: area represents angular displacement

questions.stemHtml: Of the graphs introduced in Question 2, which has the greatest average angular acceleration, [asset:image01252.jpeg]
questions.stemText: Of the graphs introduced in Question 2, which has the greatest average angular acceleration?
questions.solution: Average angular acceleration is $\bar{\alpha}=(\omega_f-\omega_i)/\Delta t$. Graphs C and E both change from 0 to 1 over the same time interval, so they tie for the greatest average angular acceleration. The answer is E.
skillTags: Use endpoints rather than instantaneous slope
questions.trainingFocus: Distinguishing average angular acceleration from the changing slope of a curve

questions.stemHtml: Of the graphs introduced in Question 2, which has the smallest average angular velocity?
questions.stemText: Of the graphs introduced in Question 2, which has the smallest average angular velocity?
questions.solution: Average angular velocity is $\bar{\omega}=\Delta\theta/\Delta t=(1/\Delta t)\int\omega\,dt$. In graph A, the positive and negative signed areas cancel, giving zero average angular velocity. Every other graph has a positive area, so A is the smallest.
skillTags: Distinguish average value from average acceleration
questions.trainingFocus: Signed graphical area and the average value of a time-dependent quantity

questions.stemHtml: Imagine a truck driving on the xy-plane in the +y-direction. If it is slowing down, in what direction is the angular acceleration of its wheels?
questions.stemText: A truck drives on the xy-plane in the positive y-direction. If it is slowing down, in what direction is the angular acceleration of its wheels?
questions.solution: For rolling in the $+y$ direction, the wheel's angular velocity points in the $-x$ direction. Slowing down means the angular acceleration opposes the angular velocity, so $\vec{\alpha}$ points in the $+x$ direction. The answer is A.
skillTags: Relate slowing rotation to angular acceleration direction
questions.trainingFocus: Three-dimensional direction reasoning for rolling wheels

questions.stemHtml: A disk in a horizontal plane is rotating at constant angular speed about a vertical axis through its center. Consider point A at the edge and point B halfway from the center to the edge. What is the linear speed of point A?
questions.stemText: A disk rotates at constant angular speed. Point A is at the edge and point B is halfway from the center to the edge. What is the linear speed of point A?

choices.label: A
choices.html: The same as the linear speed of point B
choices.text: The same as the linear speed of point B

choices.label: B
choices.html: Twice the linear speed of point B
choices.text: Twice the linear speed of point B

choices.label: C
choices.html: Half the linear speed of point B
choices.text: Half the linear speed of point B

choices.label: D
choices.html: Four times the linear speed of point B
choices.text: Four times the linear speed of point B

choices.label: E
choices.html: It depends on the angular speed of the disk
choices.text: It depends on the angular speed of the disk

questions.solution: For a rigid disk, $v=r\omega$. Point A is at twice the radius of point B while both points share the same $\omega$, so $v_A=2v_B$. The answer is B.
questions.trainingFocus: The radius dependence of tangential speed

questions.stemHtml: A cable is wrapped around a uniform solid cylinder of mass M and radius R that can rotate about an axis through its center. The moment of inertia is [asset:image01253.jpeg] If the cable is pulled tangentially with force F, what is the linear acceleration of a point on the cable?
questions.stemText: A cable is wrapped around a uniform solid cylinder of mass M and radius R. Its moment of inertia is I = 1/2 MR². The cable is pulled tangentially with force F. What is the linear acceleration of a point on the cable?
questions.solution: The applied torque is $\tau=FR$. Using $\tau=I\alpha$ and $I=\tfrac12MR^2$ gives $\alpha=2F/(MR)$. With no slipping between cable and cylinder, $a=\alpha R=2F/M$. The answer is B.
skillTags: Use a standard moment of inertia
questions.trainingFocus: Linking torque, angular acceleration, and the cable's linear acceleration

questions.stemHtml:
Two forces, F1 and F2, are applied to the bar shown. What is the net torque about the left end of the bar?
[asset:image01254.jpeg]
questions.stemText: Two forces F1 and F2 are applied to a bar. What is the net torque about the left end of the bar?
questions.solution: Taking counterclockwise as positive, $F_1$ produces $+F_1\ell_1$. Only the component $F_2\sin\theta$ perpendicular to the bar produces torque, and it acts clockwise, giving $-F_2\ell_2\sin\theta$. Thus $\tau_{net}=F_1\ell_1-F_2\ell_2\sin\theta$, answer E.
questions.trainingFocus: Torque direction and the perpendicular component of an angled force

questions.stemHtml: The rotor of a centrifuge, originally at rest, is accelerated with angular acceleration α for a time interval Δt1, left at constant speed for Δt2, and then slowed with angular acceleration −α until it stops. What is the total angular displacement?
questions.stemText: A centrifuge rotor accelerates from rest, rotates at constant speed, and then slows at the same acceleration magnitude until it stops. What is the total angular displacement?
questions.solution: The peak angular speed is $\omega_{max}=\alpha\Delta t_1$. The acceleration and deceleration intervals have equal duration and equal triangular areas on an $\omega$-$t$ graph, together contributing $\alpha(\Delta t_1)^2$. The constant-speed interval contributes $\omega_{max}\Delta t_2=\alpha\Delta t_1\Delta t_2$. Their sum is choice C.
skillTags: Find area under a piecewise $\omega$-$t$ graph
Relate symmetric acceleration and deceleration intervals
questions.trainingFocus: Combining triangular and rectangular areas for multi-stage rotational motion
